candidates.stem: You work for a retailer whose demand forecasts determine store replenishment. The forecasting service already runs on Cloud Run, and successive trained releases are stored in separate Cloud Storage folders. Your team is migrating the release catalog to Agent Platform Model Registry. You want to keep releases grouped by forecasting model while minimizing catalog clutter. You also want a stable reference to the approved release while minimizing changes for catalog consumers. Which approach should you use?

options.label: A
options.text: Record releases as artifacts in Agent Platform ML Metadata and group them in a forecasting context. Store the approved artifact identifier as a context attribute.

options.label: B
options.text: Import each release as a version of one Agent Platform Model Registry model. Retain version IDs and move an approved alias to the selected version after each approval.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a separate Model Registry model for every forecasting release. Label each model with its forecasting family and approval state, and have catalog consumers select releases using those labels.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep one registered model version and replace artifacts at its Cloud Storage location after approval. Record previous release locations in the model description for catalog consumers.

plan.engineering_decision: Choose how to organize successive forecasting releases and reference the approved release in Agent Platform Model Registry.
plan.business_consequence: Preserve release traceability and simplify approval changes for teams consuming the forecasting model catalog.
plan.existing_system: You work for a retailer whose demand forecasts determine store replenishment. mistakes.action: Create a separate Model Registry model for every release, attach labels identifying the forecasting family and approval state, and have catalog consumers select releases by those labels.
mistakes.scenario_reason: Separate model resources fragment the release family. Labels require custom selection logic instead of providing a model version alias that consumers can keep referencing as approvals change.

mistakes.action: Maintain one registered model version, replace the artifacts at its Cloud Storage location after each approval, and record previous release locations in the model description.
mistakes.scenario_reason: Replacing artifacts collapses distinct releases into one registered identity. A description listing old locations does not establish separate registry versions that consumers can inspect and reference.

mistakes.action: Record releases as artifacts in Agent Platform ML Metadata, group them in a forecasting context, and store the approved artifact identifier as a context attribute.
mistakes.scenario_reason: ML Metadata organizes artifact lineage, but this approach substitutes custom metadata conventions for Model Registry model versions and aliases, increasing catalog management and consumer integration work.

candidates.stem: You manage product recommendations for an online retailer. The storefront calls a Cloud Run service, and returning customers often request recommendations several times before buying. Your team has prepared a candidate model that uses less compute per request. Purchases are tracked per customer, so the team needs to compare model versions before adopting the cheaper candidate. You want to estimate the candidate's effect on customer purchases while minimizing changes to the running serving setup. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure Cloud Run to split traffic evenly between the current and candidate revisions. Let the platform route each recommendation request, record which revision handled it, and compare customer purchase conversion and serving cost attributed to each revision.

options.label: B
options.text: Mirror production recommendation requests to a separate candidate Cloud Run service. Keep displaying the current model's recommendations, compare prediction agreement and serving cost on the same customer inputs, and promote the candidate when those measurements indicate acceptable performance.

options.label: C
options.text: Send all production traffic to the candidate Cloud Run revision. Compare customer purchase conversion and serving cost with the previous week's results, keep the candidate if those metrics improve, and restore the previous revision if customer purchase conversion declines.

options.label: D
options.text: Deploy the candidate as a tagged Cloud Run revision. Randomly assign customers to two persistent groups in the application, route each group to its revision URL across sessions, and compare customer purchase conversion and serving cost between the groups.

plan.engineering_decision: Choose a canary rollout strategy that compares a smaller recommendation model with the running version using concurrent production traffic.
plan.business_consequence: Faster hotel recommendations could improve the customer experience, but promoting a weaker model could reduce completed bookings.
plan.existing_system: You manage a hotel recommendation service running on an Agent Platform endpoint. Your team has prepared a smaller candidate model to reduce response times. Application events identify which model generated each recommendation and whether the customer completed a booking. You want to reduce recommendation latency while minimizing declines in booking conversion. You want to compare versions on live customer traffic while minimizing changes to the serving system. What should you do?
decisive_constraints: You want to reduce recommendation latency while minimizing declines in booking conversion.
You want to compare versions on live customer traffic while minimizing changes to the serving system.
plan.best_action: Deploy the candidate alongside the current model on the existing Agent Platform endpoint, route a small traffic share to it, and increase that share after comparing booking conversion and response latency.

mistakes.action: Migrate both recommendation models to GKE, configure weighted routing through an ingress, and gradually increase candidate traffic after comparing booking conversion and response latency across the two separately managed model services.
mistakes.scenario_reason: GKE provides a plausible weighted rollout architecture, but migrating the running service adds infrastructure and routing work when the proposed managed endpoint traffic split can handle the comparison.

mistakes.action: Deploy the candidate on a separate Agent Platform endpoint, mirror production requests to both versions, and choose the candidate after comparing prediction differences and response latency on identical inputs.
mistakes.scenario_reason: Mirroring can compare predictions and latency, but customers only see the current model's recommendations. It cannot establish the candidate's effect on completed bookings.

mistakes.action: Replace the current model with the candidate on the existing Agent Platform endpoint, compare overall booking conversion and response latency with last week's averages, and roll back if either deteriorates.
mistakes.scenario_reason: Full replacement exposes all customers immediately, and historical averages confound model effects with changes in customer traffic or hotel availability. A concurrent baseline makes the comparison more reliable.

proof.reason: The supplied docs don't establish A's decisive capability: deploying two recommendation models on one Agent Platform model endpoint and controlling their traffic percentages independently. The revisions documentation covers agents, while rolling deployment documents automatic replacement rather than a controlled canary comparison. Consequently, B's rejection based on an equivalent managed endpoint capability and A's uniquely best status remain unverified. C and D have sound engineering tradeoffs, but the decision needs replacement or direct model-endpoint traffic-splitting evidence.

candidates.stem: You are operating a product-image search service whose embedding model runs on a GPU-backed Agent Platform endpoint. During shopping peaks, monitoring shows growing request queues and high GPU utilization, but CPU utilization remains low and replicas stay at their minimum. The autoscaling policy uses CPU utilization, and the maximum replica count has spare capacity. Accelerator demand drops between peaks. You want serving capacity to follow demand while minimizing changes to serving operations. How should you address this issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Migrate the embedding model to a GPU-backed GKE cluster and configure a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler using GPU utilization to adjust serving capacity during shopping peaks.

options.label: B
options.text: Raise the existing Agent Platform endpoint's minimum replica count to cover peak search demand, retaining CPU-utilization autoscaling to keep that capacity available between shopping peaks.

options.label: C
options.text: Switch the existing Agent Platform endpoint to GPU-utilization autoscaling, retaining its replica bounds so capacity increases and decreases with accelerator demand.

options.label: D
options.text: Increase the existing Agent Platform endpoint's maximum replica count, retaining CPU-utilization autoscaling so the deployment has room to add capacity during shopping peaks.

plan.engineering_decision: Choose an autoscaling signal that makes the existing serving backend respond to its GPU-bound workload.
plan.business_consequence: Insufficient replicas delay product-image searches during shopping peaks, while permanently provisioning peak capacity increases idle accelerator cost.
plan.existing_system: You are operating a product-image search service whose embedding model runs on a GPU-backed Agent Platform endpoint. Monitoring shows growing request queues and busy GPUs during shopping peaks, but CPU utilization remains low and replica count stays at its minimum. The autoscaling policy tracks CPU load, and the replica ceiling has spare capacity. You want to keep searches responsive while minimizing idle accelerator cost. You want to handle growing throughput while minimizing changes to serving operations. How should you address this issue?
decisive_constraints: You want to keep searches responsive while minimizing idle accelerator cost.

mistakes.action: Increase the endpoint's maximum replica limit and retain CPU utilization as the autoscaling signal so additional capacity can handle rising image-search traffic.
mistakes.scenario_reason: The existing ceiling already has spare capacity. Raising it does not trigger additional replicas when the selected CPU signal remains low.

mistakes.action: Move the image-embedding model to GKE and implement GPU-aware pod autoscaling to handle increased search throughput on a separately managed serving cluster.
mistakes.scenario_reason: This introduces a serving migration and cluster operations when the existing managed endpoint can scale using GPU utilization.

mistakes.action: Raise the endpoint's minimum replica count to cover peak image-search traffic and keep those replicas available throughout the day to absorb sudden demand.
mistakes.scenario_reason: A permanent peak-capacity floor can relieve queues but pays for idle GPUs between shopping peaks instead of scaling with accelerator demand.
